blocks.passage:
Sanctions compliance is a moving target. Lists are updated weekly, rules are expanded suddenly, and the same name can be fine in one country and forbidden in another. A trade compliance team that has been doing the same check for three years may be doing the wrong check today.

In practice, compliance works like layers. First, every new counterparty is screened against the main watchlists. Second, every payment and shipment is screened again at the moment it moves — because lists change. Third, any unusual pattern is escalated to a specialist.

The companies that get into real trouble are almost never the ones that tried hard and made a mistake. They are the ones that stopped checking, or checked once and never again.

items.q: Why is sanctions compliance called "a moving target"?
options: Lists are updated weekly and rules expand suddenly
items.why: "Lists are updated weekly, rules are expanded suddenly."

items.q: What is the first layer of compliance?
options: Screening every new counterparty against the main watchlists
items.why: "First, every new counterparty is screened against the main watchlists."

items.q: Why is every payment and shipment screened again at the moment it moves?
items.why: "every payment and shipment is screened again at the moment it moves — because lists change."

items.q: What happens to an unusual pattern?
options: It is escalated to a specialist
items.why: "any unusual pattern is escalated to a specialist."

items.q: Which companies get into real trouble, according to the text?
options: Those that tried hard and made a mistake
Those that stopped checking, or checked once and never again
items.why: "the ones that stopped checking, or checked once and never again."

audio.text:
I know this is confusing, so let me explain why last week's screening passed and this week's did not — for the exact same counterparty.

Nothing about the counterparty changed. What changed is the list. A new name was added to the sanctions watchlist on Monday, and it's linked to one of the owners behind this company. Last week that link didn't trigger anything, because the name wasn't on the list yet. This week it does.

This is exactly why we screen at the moment of every payment, not just once when we onboard a client. If we only checked at the start, we'd have shipped this week completely unaware, and that's how good companies end up in serious trouble — not through malice, through going stale.

So here's what we do now. We do not process this payment. We freeze it, and I escalate it to our sanctions specialist today. They'll confirm whether it's a true match or a false positive with a similar name.

Until they clear it, nothing moves. Better a delayed payment than a sanctions breach.

items.q: Why did this week's screening fail when last week's passed?
options: The list changed — a new name was added on Monday
items.why: "Nothing about the counterparty changed. What changed is the list."

items.q: What is the new name linked to?
options: One of the owners behind this company
items.why: "it's linked to one of the owners behind this company."

items.q: Why does the team screen at the moment of every payment?
options: Because lists change — checking only at onboarding would miss updates
items.why: "This is exactly why we screen at the moment of every payment, not just once when we onboard a client."

items.q: What does the team do with this payment?
options: Freeze it and escalate to the sanctions specialist
items.why: "We freeze it, and I escalate it to our sanctions specialist today."

items.q: What is Charlotte's closing principle?
options: Better a delayed payment than a sanctions breach
items.why: "Better a delayed payment than a sanctions breach."

items.q: A **counterparty** is…
options: the other party in a transaction
items.why: Counterparty = contraparte.

items.q: **Screening** against a watchlist means…
options: checking a name against a list of restricted parties
items.why: Screening = triagem contra listas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "An unusual pattern should be **___** to a specialist."
items.why: To escalate = escalar.

items.q: A **false positive** is…
options: an apparent match that turns out not to be the sanctioned party
items.why: False positive = alarme falso (nome parecido, não a mesma pessoa).

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Compliance works in **___** — screen at onboarding and again at each payment."
items.why: Layered check = verificação em camadas.

items.q: "A team that checks once can **go stale**." To go stale means to…
items.why: Go stale = ficar desatualizado.

items.q: "Let's **freeze** the payment for now." To freeze a payment means to…
items.why: Freeze = congelar, deter temporariamente.

items.q: "We'd have shipped **unaware**." To do something unaware means to…
options: do it without knowing an important fact
items.why: Unaware = sem saber.

items.q: "Until they **clear it**, nothing moves." To clear something means to…
options: approve it as safe to proceed
items.why: Clear = liberar após verificação.

items.q: "Sanctions rules can **catch you out**." To catch someone out means to…
options: expose them in a mistake they didn't see coming
items.why: Catch out = pegar em falta, surpreender no erro.
